title: Postoperative Outcomes of Digital Nerve Coaptations Using a Sutureless Coaptation Device
official: Postoperative Outcomes of Digital Nerve Coaptations Using a Sutureless Coaptation Device
summary:
Injuries to the small nerves in the fingers are common and can affect feeling, cause pain, and limit hand function. These nerves are usually repaired during surgery by carefully stitching the nerve ends together. While this approach often restores basic protective feeling, many people do not regain normal sensation in the injured finger, and recovery can be unpredictable.

This study looks at the postoperative outcomes of a newer surgical coaptation device called Nerve Tape, which allows surgeons to reconnect injured finger nerves without using stitches. Instead, the device gently holds the nerve ends together using a flexible wrap designed to support healing while minimizing additional trauma to the nerve. Early laboratory and clinical studies suggest that this approach may shorten surgery time and provide stable nerve repair, but more information is needed about how patients recover after this type of repair.

The purpose of this study is to better understand how patients do after finger nerve repair using this suture-free device. Specifically, the study examines how well feeling returns, how much pain patients experience, and how hand function improves over time. Sensation, pain levels, and hand function are measured during routine follow-up visits over the first six months after surgery. The information gained from this study will help improve knowledge about outcomes after finger nerve repair and support future research comparing different repair methods.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with complete traumatic digit nerve transections between the MCP and the DIP joints, suitable for direct end-to-end coaptation that are treated with Nerve Tape as part of their standard clinical care
* Age between 18 and 67 years
* Trauma occurred in the previous 72 hours
* Able to provide informed consent
* Use of Nerve Tape for standard care surgical procedure for digital nerve repair

Exclusion Criteria:

* Nerve lesions proximal to the MCP joint of the digital nerve that would be treated with NerveTape
* Nerve injuries with a gap requiring auto- or allograft interposition
* Amputated or avascular fingers
* Active infection of the wound
* Known pre-existing impaired sensibility of the injured finger or the opposite side
* Allergy to the contents of Nerve Tape
* Known immunodeficiency
* Inability to provide informed consent
* Surgeon decision to not use Nerve Tape during digital nerve repair
